title: Leicester confirm signing of Ayoze Pérez from Newcastle for £30m
trail: Leicester City have completed the signing of Ayoze Pérez from Newcastle for around £30m
body: Leicester City have completed the signing of Ayoze Pérez from Newcastle for around £30m. The 25-year-old striker has signed a four-year contract with Leicester after they activated the buy-out clause in his contract and beat off competition from a number of leading European clubs. Leicester will now press ahead with their attempt to sign Youri Tielemans from Monaco. Tielemans is keen to move to the King Power Stadium after enjoying a successful loan spell last season but it is understood that Leicester and Monaco are still some way apart when it comes to their valuation of the 22-year-old midfielder. Leicester recognise that it will take a club-record deal to sign Tielemans but the asking price is currently upward of £40m and there may well need to be a compromise to get the transfer through. Including Adrien Silva as a makeweight – the Portuguese moved to Monaco on loan last season as part of the deal that saw Tielemans go the other way – would appeal to Leicester but the French club have made it clear that they want any transfer for the Belgium international to be straight cash. That is not to say that Monaco may not return for Silva at a later date in what feels like a game of brinkmanship. The arrival of Pérez, meanwhile, will increase Leicester’s attacking options and also raises the prospect of him playing alongside Jamie Vardy. Leicester have tried and failed to find a player to fulfil that second striker role in recent years, with Kelechi Iheanacho enduring two difficult seasons following his arrival from Manchester City. Iheanacho, however, is expected to stay at Leicester. Pérez scored 12 Premier League goals last season, with his excellent partnership with Salomón Rondón helping Newcastle to pull away from the relegation zone. Newcastle will make a large profit on a player signed from Tenerife for £1.5m in 2014, but his departure also leaves a sizeable hole to fill. Pérez has been Newcastle’s top scorer in all competitions in each of the past two seasons, getting 13 goals in the last campaign and also reaching double figures the year before. His versatility, together with his age and his excellent form for Newcastle in the second half of the season, when he scored 11 goals, made him an attractive proposition for Leicester and their manager, Brendan Rodgers. “I think Ayoze will be a wonderful addition to the squad,” Rodgers said. “He’s quick, has a good eye for goal and he’s experienced in the Premier League too. I think he’s a player who will excite our supporters.”
